what_its_for: This pill is used to prevent pregnancy (birth control). It also helps treat moderate acne in women who are at least 14 years old and have started their periods. In addition, it may be used to treat a condition called PMDD (premenstrual dysphoric disorder), which causes severe mood and physical symptoms before your period. The levomefolate calcium (a form of folate/folic acid) in this pill helps build up folate levels in your body, which is important if you become pregnant after stopping the pill.
how_to_take: Take one tablet by mouth every day at the same time each day. Swallow the tablet whole with or without food. If you feel nauseated, try taking it with food or at bedtime. Take the tablets in the exact order shown on your pill pack — do not skip or rearrange the order. Start on the first day of your period or on the first Sunday after your period begins, as directed by your doctor. Use a backup method of birth control (such as condoms) for the first 7 days if you do not start on the first day of your period.
dosing: Take one tablet daily for 28 days, then start a new pack the very next day. The pack contains 24 active pink pills (with hormones and folate) and 4 light orange reminder pills (folate only, no hormones). Take the reminder pills to stay in the habit of taking a pill every day. Your period will usually occur during the week you take the reminder pills.
missed_dose: If you miss 1 active pink pill: Take it as soon as you remember, even if it means taking 2 pills in one day. No backup birth control is needed. If you miss 2 active pink pills in a row in Week 1 or Week 2: Take 2 pills on the day you remember and 2 pills the next day, then continue one pill per day. Use a backup method (like condoms) for 7 days. If you miss 2 active pink pills in a row in Week 3, or miss 3 or more active pink pills in a row at any time: Throw away the rest of the pack and start a new pack that same day. Use a backup birth control method for 7 days. If you miss any light orange reminder pills, simply throw them away and continue with your next pill. Whenever you miss pills, you may have spotting or light bleeding, and you could get pregnant. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store at room temperature between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store in the bathroom. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused pills down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of them.
what_to_avoid: Do not smoke while taking this medication, especially if you are over 35 years old — smoking greatly increases your risk of serious heart and blood vessel problems. Avoid taking potassium supplements, potassium-sparing diuretics (water pills), or large amounts of potassium-rich salt substitutes without checking with your doctor first, since drospirenone can raise potassium levels. Tell all your doctors and your pharmacist about every medicine you take, including over-the-counter drugs and herbal supplements. Some medications (such as rifampin, certain seizure medicines, St. John's Wort, and some HIV drugs) can make this pill less effective at preventing pregnancy. This pill does NOT protect you from HIV or other sexually transmitted infections (STIs). Use condoms to reduce that risk.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience any of the following warning signs — remember the word ACHES: Abdominal pain (severe); Chest pain or shortness of breath; Headache (severe, sudden); Eye problems such as blurred or lost vision; Severe leg pain or swelling in the calf. Also call your doctor if you notice: yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice); breast lump; severe depression or mood changes; unusual vaginal bleeding; signs of high potassium such as muscle weakness or irregular heartbeat; or if you think you might be pregnant.
when_it_works: For birth control: This pill is most effective when taken correctly every day. It begins to protect against pregnancy after 7 days if you start mid-cycle; it works from day one if you start on the first day of your period. For acne and PMDD: It may take several weeks to a few months before you notice improvement. Be patient and keep taking it as directed.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Do not use this medication if you are pregnant. Stop taking it if you become pregnant. Breastfeeding: This pill is generally not recommended while breastfeeding because hormones can pass into breast milk and may reduce your milk supply. Talk to your doctor about other options. Teenagers: This medication can be used in girls who have already started their periods. It should not be used before the first period. Older women: This medication is not intended for use after menopause. Women over 35 who smoke should not use this pill. Kidney, liver, or adrenal disease: Tell your doctor if you have any of these conditions, as this pill may not be safe for you due to its effect on potassium levels.
